rows.title: Nernst Equation Calculator
rows.scope: Nernst cell potential E = E° - (RT/nF) ln Q for the same balanced redox reaction, with E° applicable at the supplied positive kelvin temperature and a positive safe-integer electron transfer count n. Q is a positive dimensionless activity quotient relative to standard states, with pure solid/liquid activities taken as unity; concentration substitution requires justified ideal behavior. The engine fixes R = 8.31446261815324 J/(mol K) and F = 96485.33212 C/mol; it does not compute activities, temperature corrections to E°, kinetics, overpotential or junction potentials.
rows.additionalDomain: standardPotential signed; temperatureKelvin>0; electronCount positive safe integer <=9007199254740991; reactionQuotient>0
rows.assumptionsAudit: Dimensionless activity quotient and E0 at supplied T for same balanced reaction; no activity/E0 temperature correction. Cancellation near E=0 has no relative-error guarantee.
rows.publisherRelevanceAudit: OpenStax17.4 Nernst;13.2 relative dimensionless Q; IUPAC activity; NIST constants support applicability, displayed ellipses do not establish all fixed engine digits; F is truncated.

sourceBinding.supports: Nernst form, transferred electrons, positive absolute temperature, and relative dimensionless Q are supported by OpenStax. NIST supplies SI units and exact constants with displayed decimal prefixes. IUPAC activity definition explicitly relates relative activity to chemical potential and the choice of standard state.
sourceBinding.gap: NIST returned decimal values use ellipses, not every engine digit. Immutable code fixes R=8.31446261815324 and truncated F=96485.33212. Q input is assumed to be activity-based; no activity coefficients or E° temperature-dependence are computed. Safe integer electron count is a conservative capture policy; historical fractional engine inputs replay unchanged.

rows.title: Beer-Lambert Law Calculator
rows.scope: Decadic absorbance A = εbc using molar absorption coefficient ε in L/(mol cm), optical path b in cm and concentration c in mol/L. Assumes collimated monochromatic radiation, a homogeneous isotropic absorbing medium, and valid linear response at the chosen wavelength; excludes scattering, stray light, concentration-dependent interactions, speciation changes and detector saturation. Zero factor gives zero absorbance within the ideal mathematical model.
rows.assumptionsAudit: Decadic A; epsilon L/(mol cm), path cm, concentration mol/L; monochromatic homogeneous linear regime; zeros mathematical limits.
rows.publisherRelevanceAudit: IUPAC B00626 explicitly defines law and units; no irrelevant OpenStax6.1 claim.

sourceBinding.supports: IUPAC explicitly gives A=epsilon*c*l, collimated monochromatic radiation, homogeneous isotropic medium, cm path and mol/dm3 concentration with dm3/(mol cm) absorption coefficient.
sourceBinding.gap: OpenStax Chemistry2e section 6.1 was inspected but contains no Beer-Lambert definition; it is not cited as applicable evidence. IUPAC provides the applicable primary definition. Instrument linearity, scattering and speciation are not evaluated.
